subject: POC: Orchard AI - integration owners, success criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orchard.ai>, Priya Desai <priya@orchard.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: POC: Orchard AI - integration owners, success criteria & next steps

Thanks again for the demo and the time today — great conversation. Per our discovery, I wanted to capture the proposed POC scope, owners, and concrete success criteria so we can lock the kickoff and the technical handoffs. I attached a short POC scope doc (20280612-Orchard-POC-Scope.pdf). Please review and confirm.

High-level POC objective:
- Validate Redwood inference in Orchard AI's production-like pipeline for document classification and entity extraction, including streaming inference and tool-calling to your enrichment service.

Success criteria (we should be able to mark these pass/fail at the end of the trial):
1) Latency: median response latency under 220ms for <512 token requests for synchronous API routes, and stable sub-500ms tail for streaming endpoints under expected load.
2) Accuracy: classification F1 >= 0.88 on the agreed 500-sample evaluation set (you to provide).
3) Integration: SDK-based integration (Node/Python) exercising streaming + tool-calling with one enrichment webhook implemented.
4) Cost baseline: estimate of per-1k token cost with recommended batching/quantization profile documented.

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): kickoff + access (API keys, test dataset, whitelist IPs)
- Week 1: SDK integration + streaming tests (internal dev environment)
- Week 2: End-to-end run against eval set, metrics collection, and short wrap call to review pass/fail

Owners (proposed):
- Redwood technical lead: Ben Carter (integration + SDK support)
- Redwood product/ops: Marissa Cole (metrics, rollout plan)
- Orchard technical lead: Samir Patel (access to test data and enrichment endpoints)
- Orchard PM: Priya Desai (acceptance, scheduling)

Open questions / asks for Orchard before kickoff:
- Confirm who will provide the 500-sample eval set and the format (JSONL preferred).
- Confirm whether enrichment tool-calls need to be proxied through your VPC (if so we need IP ranges).
- Any restrictions on synthetic data vs. PII in the test set?

Next steps: please reply with availability for a 45-minute kickoff (I propose Thu 20 Jun, 09:00am PT) and confirm the two items above.

Attachments: 20280612-Orchard-POC-Scope.pdf (pdf)

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: Orchard AI - integration owners, success criteria & next steps

Quick alignment from engineering side — we can commit to the proposed timeline and will prepare the following artifacts before kickoff:
- Redwood SDK quickstart (Node + Python) with a streaming example and tool-calling shim (see attached proto-config.yaml for the sample route mapping).
- Example route names: /v1/generate, /v1/generate-stream (websocket-compatible), and /v1/tool/call for the enrichment handshake.
- Model recommendation: start with rwd-2.7b-opt (quantized) for latency/cost balance; fallback to rwd-1.0-std if you need higher determinism.

Notes/risks:
- If Orchard requires the enrichment endpoint to be in a private VPC with no public egress, we'll need a temporary tunnel or a small NATed proxy for the trial (or we can run a lightweight mock on your side).
- For the accuracy eval, please send a sample JSONL (id, text, expected_label) and we will run a holdout.

I've attached proto-config.yaml to show how the streaming and tool-calling steps are wired. I'll be the primary on-call for SDK questions during Week 1.

—Ben

Thanks Tessa — this looks good and matches what we discussed. A few items from our side before kickoff: 

1) Data residency: the eval set will be US-only, but we need confirmation that test data will not be logged to any external analytics by default. Can Redwood confirm retention/telemetry defaults for POC keys?
2) We will provide the 500-sample JSONL by EOD Monday (18 Jun).
3) For enrichment tool-calls, we prefer not to expose the live endpoint. We can host a mock enrichment service in our staging VPC and provide a temporary tunnel or a signed URL for the trial.

We are available for the kickoff on Thu 20 Jun 09:00am PT — please send the calendar invite. Also, please send any DocuSign/engagement terms if needed for the reserved trial capacity.
